sentences.text: Ms. K.M. Monika - Advocate with Shri Ranjeet Singh Raw  Advocate for appellant.
Shri Vijay Sundaram - Public Prosecutor for respondent 1.
Heard on I.A. No.26321/2024 , fourth repeat application under Section 430 of BNSS, 2023 (389(1) of Cr.P.C) for suspension of sentence on behalf of appellant - Rajat.

2. Appellant is facing sentence by virtue of judgment dated 20.10.2022 passed by the VIth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, (POCSO) Act, District- Bhind passed in ST No.133/2021 whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:-
 Section Imprisonment Fin  376(3) of IPC 20 Years' RI Rs.5,000/- with de  3/4 of POCSO Act 20 Years' RI Rs.5,000/- with de  366-A of IPC 5 Years' RI Rs.5,000/- with de  323 of IPC 6 Months' RI Rs.5,00/- with def 3.

entities.text: VIth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, (POCSO) Act, District- Bhind
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that trial Court erred in convicting the appellant and awarding jail sentence without appreciating the evidence and material available on record.
Appellant has suffered 3 years and 10 months of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.

It is further submitted that as per own allegation of prosecutrix, appellant and prosecutrix shared emotional proximity and course of events as 2 CRA-10544-2022 unfolded indicates peculiar nature of allegation.
It is highly improbable that prosecutrix stayed with appellant and his friends for a considerable period of time (for some hours) without raising alarm.
If evidence is seen with the medical opinion and DNA report, then it clearly establishes the false nature of allegations.
Age of prosecutrix is not established by the prosecution to bring home the analogy that prosecutrix was minor.
She was major and this aspect has been ignored by learned trial Court.
Material contradictions and omissions exist in the testimony of prosecutrix and other witnesses.
Hearing of appeal shall take some time.
He has a good case on merits.
Fine amount has already been deposited.
He undertakes to abide by the terms and conditions as imposed by this Court.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of allegations and evidence surfaced as well as period of custody, learned counsel for appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
4. Learned counsel for State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of application.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties at length and considered the arguments advanced by them.
6.

Considering the submissions and the arguments advanced by counsel for the parties as well as looking to the nature of allegations against the present appellant, without commenting on the merits of the case as there is no possibility of early hearing of this criminal appeal before this Court, hence,
I.A.No.26321/2024 i s allowed.

Appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the 3 CRA-10544-2022 concerned trial Court
, appellant's jail sentence shall remain suspended till disposal of this appeal.
Appellant is further directed to remain present before the Registry of this Court on 18.06.2025 and, thereafter, on such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry.
7. A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
8. Certified copy as per rules/directions.

(ANAND PATHAK) (HI  JUDGE J  *VJ*
